text:
rachel.docs: Quick heads-up: we're changing the telemetry default for the SDK CLI. This affects the CLI `init` and `telemetry` helpers and the docs/examples that reference them.

TL;DR: telemetry will become opt-in by default for new installs (prompt at first-run) instead of opt-out. Existing users keep current setting. We'll update docs and SDKs in one coordinated release. Migration window: immediate for docs; 90 days for any server-side metrics relying on CLI telemetry.

Why: privacy review flagged that a developer-first opt-in is a better pattern internationally, and enterprise customers requested explicit consent flows. We also want clearer docs about what data is collected and how it's used.

What changes in practice:
- CLI behavior: new installs will show a one-line prompt on first-run (`Enable anonymous telemetry to help improve SDKs? (y/N)`). No data is sent unless user confirms.
- Existing installs: no change. If customers have `sdk.telemetry.enabled=true` already, we do nothing.
- Docs: we'll replace examples that assume telemetry is enabled and add an "opt-in" snippet and a short privacy table.
- Hosted metrics: some build-telemetry dashboards will need annotation to mark data as "pre-change" for 90 days.

tom.sdk: Implementation notes: JS and Python CLI packages will ship minor releases. We'll add a simple interactive prompt (non-blocking in CI if `CI=true`). Example (pseudocode):

```bash
# first-run prompt
Enable anonymous telemetry to help improve Redwood SDKs? [y/N]
# store choice in ~/.redwood/config.json
```

We'll also add a non-interactive env override `REDWOOD_CLI_TELEMETRY=true|false` for automation.

lena.privacy: We'll need a short privacy FAQ section: exact fields collected, retention, and where to opt-out. Also legal wants the new wording for the prompt and the link to the privacy policy. I'll draft language and push to the migration doc.

carlos.support: Heads-up from support: enterprise customers often set `sdk.telemetry.enabled=true` via config management. I'll add a KB article showing how to propagate the env var in common tooling (Ansible, Helm, Terraform). Also prepare a canned response explaining that no historic telemetry will be deleted by default but accounts can request removal.

jen.product: Can we surface opt-in banners on the docs site and in the Console docs pages? A short banner and a clear link to the FAQ will help AMs. Also, product wants a short metric about how many new installs accept telemetry vs decline (to baseline after rollout).

devops: For internal infra: we should add a rollout annotation to dashboards and a short script to tag historical telemetry so that the analytics team can compute pre/post opt-in rates. I'll open a PR to add a `telemetry_policy_change` tag to our pipeline.

ops-bot: Reminder: docs site rebuild scheduled Mon 01:00 UTC after SDK patches land. Expect ~10m of build time.

rachel.docs: Docs migration checklist (short):
- [x] Draft opt-in prompt copy (lena)
- [x] Add CLI flag + env var docs (tom)
- [ ] Update CLI examples to show opt-in flow (rachel/tom)
- [ ] Publish privacy FAQ and retention table (lena)
- [ ] KB article for enterprise rollout & env var propagation (carlos)
- [ ] Add banner and AM one-pager (jen)
- [ ] Analytics annotation + dashboard tagging (devops)

If you own one of the unchecked items, drop a :thumbsup: and paste the PR/issue link. We plan to ship SDK patches and docs updates together next Wednesday. Thanks!
